eyebrow: Python for Data Science · Chapter 6, Lesson 29
subtitle: A web address that returns data instead of a page — always fresh, no manual downloads.

code:
import requests

url = "https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users"
resp = requests.get(url, timeout=10)

resp.status_code    # 200
data = resp.json()  # a list of 10 dictionaries
caption: timeout stops your code from waiting forever. 200 is success, 404 not found, 401/403 not authorized.

code:
df = pd.json_normalize(data)
df[["id", "name", "address.city"]].head(3)
#   id            name   address.city
# 0  1   Leanne Graham     Gwenborough
caption: Nested dicts like address.geo flatten into dotted column names — json_normalize from Lesson 27 again.
Pass filters as a dictionary rather than gluing them onto the URL string yourself.

code:
frames = []
for page in (1, 2, 3):
    r = requests.get(url, params={"_page": page, "_limit": 10}, timeout=10)
    r.raise_for_status()
    frames.append(pd.DataFrame(r.json()))
posts = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)   # (30, 4)
caption: raise_for_status() raises loudly on any 4xx/5xx — far better than silently building a DataFrame from an error.

titlePlain: Habits That Keep You Out of

eyebrow: API keys — keep them out of your code
code:
import os
token = os.environ["API_TOKEN"]
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
r = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=10)
caption: Never paste a key into a notebook or commit it — read it from an environment variable.
